name: Agent Repo Workflow (clone + run agent against a prompt)
info:
Reusable clone/fetch + agent-run pipeline. Fully generic: it has no knowledge of issues/PRs/etc -- callers supply a `context` object and a prompt template, and any extra fields the caller puts on `context` are automatically available to the template.

Input msg must carry:
- `msg.context` ({host, owner, repo, model, ...anything else the caller's template needs}) -- only host/owner/repo/model are read by this subflow itself; everything else is opaque cargo for template rendering.
- `msg.promptTemplate` -- a string with `{{fieldName}}` placeholders resolved against `context` plus the post-clone `{{defaultBranch}}` and `{{repoSlug}}`.

Outputs:
1. Workflow log row (info/success/error) -- append to a log table.
2. Running-workflow count text.
3. Completion signal ({context}) -- fires only on full success.
4. Raw agent progress events (2nd output of the agent node) -- feed agent-log/derive-count/important-event taps.

ADT Task (ensure worktree + run agent against a prompt)
info:
M3 scope: the reusable per-task pipeline for the Agentic Development Team. Given a context and a prompt template, ensures an isolated git worktree exists (scripts/ensure-worktree.sh), gates on adt_running (global context -- see deviation note below) immediately before the agent node so a Stop is never raced past, renders the prompt, and runs the agent.

Input msg:
- msg.context = {host, owner, repo, model, kind, itemId, taskKey, phase}
- msg.promptTemplate = string with {{field}} placeholders
- msg.operation = "terminate" (+ msg.executionId) bypasses setup and goes straight to the agent node's terminate handling (M4 wires the caller side of this; M3 only builds the structural branch so it doesn't crash deploy).

Outputs:
1. completion {context, status, payload}
2. raw agent events (agent node's 2nd output, verbatim)
3. log/error rows (worktree failures, gate drops, prompt-render problems, agent errors)

DEVIATION FROM PLAN: the gate uses global.get('adt_running')/global.set, not flow.get/flow.set as the plan's prose literally says -- a subflow instance gets its own flow context, separate from the tab it's placed on, so flow.adt_running set by a tab-level inject is never visible inside the subflow. global context is required for this cross-boundary flag to work at all.

label: Agentic Development Team
info: Continuously watches a GitHub repository and keeps up to 3 agents per category (Issues, Pull Requests, Actions) busy via adt-task-subflow. Read-only against the remote -- see docs/260820_Agentic_Development_Team.md. Repo Settings group drives Host/Owner/Repository/Model + Update/Start/Stop; Start/Stop toggle the 30s scheduler. Test: injects/debug nodes are kept intentionally (same convention as Issue Control Center) for future debugging.
